gloss: to suit one well; to look natural in a role; to be a good fit

definitions.gloss: to suit one well; to look natural in a role; to be a good fit
definitions.explanation: To have grown into a role, position, or style so that it looks completely natural and well-suited. Originally from the theater, referring to how a costume looks on an actor.

examples.japanese: スーツ{姿|すがた}が{板|いた}に{着|つ}いてきた。
examples.english: He's starting to look natural in a suit.

examples.japanese: {管理職|かんりしょく}の{役割|やくわり}がすっかり{板|いた}に{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: She's completely settled into the management role.

examples.japanese: {最初|さいしょ}は{違和感|いわかん}があったが、だんだん{板|いた}に{着|つ}いてきた。
examples.english: It felt awkward at first, but it's gradually become a natural fit.

notes:
An idiomatic expression from the theater world. {板|いた} refers to the stage (boards), and the expression originally meant that an actor's performance or costume looked natural and fitting on stage.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～が{板|いた}に{着|つ}く: ~ suits one well
- ～が{板|いた}に{着|つ}いてきた: ~ is starting to look natural
- すっかり{板|いた}に{着|つ}いた: has completely settled in

USAGE:
Used as a compliment, often about someone who was new to a role or style but has grown into it. Common contexts include:
- New positions or job titles
- Clothing or appearance changes
- New roles in life (parent, teacher, leader)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {似合|にあ}う: to suit, to look good on — more general, does not imply the process of growing into something
- {様|さま}になる: to look the part — similar meaning but more colloquial
